issues.title: Exit command resolves after activity termination
issues.description: The exit command calls `activity.finish()` before `invoke.resolve()`. This creates a race condition where the activity lifecycle may terminate before the JavaScript callback receives the resolution response. This can lead to lost responses, potential crashes in the JavaScript layer when expecting a resolution that never arrives, and unreliable exit behavior. The resolution should occur before finishing the activity to ensure the response is sent back to the frontend before the Android activity is destroyed.

issues.title: Back navigation handled by both framework and plugin
issues.description: Setting `handleBackNavigation` to `true` in TauriActivity causes the Wry framework to handle back navigation, which conflicts with the AppPlugin's custom OnBackPressedCallback implementation. This creates competing back button handlers where both the framework's default behavior and the plugin's custom logic attempt to process back button events. This can result in double back navigation, skipped history entries, or inconsistent behavior when users press the back button. The value should remain `false` to allow the AppPlugin to be the sole handler of back button events as designed in the PR.

issues.title: Exit command not registered in build.rs permissions
issues.description: The Android exit command is implemented in AppPlugin.kt but is not registered in the Rust build.rs file under the core:app plugin commands list. Without registration in the PLUGINS constant, the exit command will not be accessible through the Tauri IPC bridge, making the exit functionality completely non-functional. All Tauri commands must be registered in build.rs to be callable from the frontend, as evidenced by the pattern used for register_listener and remove_listener commands which were properly added to the same list.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14133 - feat(core): back button event on Android, closes #8142

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds an Android back-button hook to Tauri's core `app` plugin. A new Kotlin `AppPlugin` installs an `OnBackPressedCallback` on the activity. If JS has registered a `back-button` listener through the existing `Plugin.trigger` channel infrastructure, the callback forwards a `canGoBack` payload to JS. Otherwise it falls back to `webView.goBack()`, or to the activity's default back handling. On the Rust side, `plugin::init` for `app` now calls `register_android_plugin("app.tauri", "AppPlugin")` in `setup`. `TauriActivity` sets `handleBackNavigation = true`, and the TS API gains `onBackButtonPress`. The PR also bumps wry 0.53.2 to 0.53.4, adds `hasListener` to `Plugin.kt`, and adds `register_listener`/`remove_listener` to the `core:app` permission set.

The idea is sound and reuses the existing listener machinery well. However, the change as written will not compile for Android: `*handle_ref` moves a non-Copy `PluginHandle` out of a shared reference. The desktop path is also broken, since `onBackButtonPress` calls `plugin:app|register_listener`, which has no Rust implementation outside Android. Beyond that, the callback is installed unconditionally for every Android app, a registered listener fully suppresses default back navigation with no TS escape hatch, and the `exit` command is unreachable. The PR's changelog advertises "exit" support that does not exist in the API.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The Android build is broken by the `*handle_ref` move in `setup` (E0507), so the PR cannot merge as-is. Calling `onBackButtonPress` on desktop or iOS also rejects at runtime because `register_listener` is only implemented in Kotlin. Those two issues are blocking. The behavioral concerns (global back-handling change, listener trapping the user, unreachable `exit`) should be resolved or explicitly accepted before merge.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, the `app` core plugin (`crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`) exposed Rust commands such as `version` and `set_dock_visibility`. Mobile plugins are Kotlin classes that Rust reaches through `PluginHandle`, and the `Plugin` base class in `mobile/android/.../plugin/Plugin.kt` already manages event listeners. JS registers a listener by calling `plugin:<name>|register_listener` through a `Channel`, and Kotlin fires events via `trigger()`. Android's back button was handled only by the default WebView/WryActivity behaviour.

This PR adds a Kotlin `AppPlugin` that owns an `OnBackPressedCallback`. The callback checks `hasListener("back-button")`. With a listener it sends `{canGoBack}` over the channel. Without one it calls `goBack()` or the default activity back action. The Rust `app` plugin registers that Kotlin class in `setup`, and the TS `onBackButtonPress` wraps `addPluginListener('app', 'back-button', ...)`. Because `setup` runs on every platform, the Android-only Kotlin code is reached through a cfg-gated block that will not compile on Android as written.
steps: Entry point: `packages/api/src/app.ts` `onBackButtonPress` calls `addPluginListener` in `core.ts`, which invokes `plugin:app|register_listener` with a Channel.
On Android, `Plugin.registerListener` (inherited by `AppPlugin`) stores the channel in the `listeners` map. The new `hasListener` helper in `Plugin.kt` reads that map.
`AppPlugin` init installs an `OnBackPressedCallback`. On back press it either forwards to JS via `trigger` (listener present) or runs `goBack` / the default activity action.
On the Rust side, `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs` `setup` registers `app.tauri.AppPlugin` and stores the handle as managed state. This block is the one that fails to compile.

`TauriActivity.kt` sets `handleBackNavigation = true`, and `build.rs`/permissions expose `register_listener`/`remove_listener` in the `core:app` default set. Desktop has no Rust handler for those commands.

findings.title: Android build fails: moving non-Copy PluginHandle out of a reference
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`, the `.setup` closure (around lines 135-143) fails to compile on Android: `*handle_ref` moves a non-Copy `PluginHandle` out of a shared reference. Replace the `handle`/`handle_ref` dance with a direct move: `let handle = api.register_android_plugin("app.tauri", "AppPlugin")?; app.manage(AppPlugin(handle));`. Also rename `_app`/`_api` to `app`/`api` since they are used under the `target_os = "android"` cfg. Do not add `Copy`/`Clone` to `PluginHandle`.

findings.title: onBackButtonPress rejects on desktop/iOS because register_listener is Android-only
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/api/src/app.ts` (`onBackButtonPress`, around lines 267-277), the function calls `addPluginListener` for `plugin:app|register_listener`, which has no Rust implementation on desktop or iOS, so the promise rejects there. Make the function safe on every platform. Either return a no-op `PluginListener` when not running on Android (check the platform via the existing mechanism in the codebase) or add platform-independent no-op `register_listener`/`remove_listener` handlers in `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`. Update the JSDoc to state the Android-only behaviour. Follow the pattern used by other mobile-only APIs in `packages/api`.

findings.title: Registered back listener traps the user with no way to fall back to default
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt`, when a `back-button` listener is registered (the `hasListener` branch around lines 30-43), the default back action is never executed, so a JS listener that does nothing traps the user. Expose a way for JS to trigger the default behaviour (for example a `@Command` that calls `webView.goBack()` when `canGoBack` and otherwise the default activity back action, plus a matching TS helper in `packages/api/src/app.ts`). Document in the TS JSDoc that a registered listener suppresses default back handling unless it calls that helper. Follow the existing command and permission patterns in `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`.

findings.title: Back-button callback installed for every Android app, changing default behaviour
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/mobile/android-codegen/TauriActivity.kt` (line 15, `override val handleBackNavigation: Boolean = true`) and `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt` (the `init` block that installs `OnBackPressedCallback`), confirm that wry's built-in back handling and AppPlugin's callback do not both run for one press. Explain in the PR why `handleBackNavigation` is needed and why the wry version was bumped. Consider installing the callback only when a back-button listener is first registered, instead of unconditionally in `init`, so apps that do not use the feature keep stock behaviour.

findings.title: exit command is unreachable and the changelog advertises it
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt`, the `@Command fun exit` (around lines 49-53) is unreachable: it has no TS binding in `packages/api/src/app.ts`, no entry in `crates/tauri/build.rs` `core:app` commands, and no permission in `crates/tauri/permissions/app/autogenerated/reference.md`. Either wire it up end to end (build.rs permission, reference doc, TS helper) or remove it. Also update `.changes/android-app-plugin.md`, which claims exit support, so it matches what ships.

findings.title: register_listener/remove_listener added to default permissions for commands that exist only on Android
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/build.rs` (the `core:app` entry, around lines 167-168), `register_listener` and `remove_listener` are marked default-allowed (`true`) even though only the Android Kotlin plugin implements them. Change the default flag to `false`, or add platform-independent handlers, so that default capabilities do not grant commands that do nothing on desktop and iOS. Regenerate `crates/tauri/permissions/app/autogenerated/reference.md` to match, following the existing entries for `set_dock_visibility`.

findings.title: Unexplained wry bump and Cargo.lock churn
findings.body:
The PR bumps `wry` from 0.53.2 to 0.53.4 and changes several unrelated transitive `windows-sys`/`windows-targets` entries in `Cargo.lock`. The PR description says nothing about why. The wry bump is presumably needed for `handleBackNavigation` on Android, but the reviewer has no way to check that from the PR. Keep unrelated lockfile churn out of feature PRs, or call out why it is required.

::diff{file="crates/tauri-runtime-wry/Cargo.toml" lines="19-21"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-runtime-wry/Cargo.toml` line 20, the wry dependency is bumped to 0.53.4 and `Cargo.lock` picks up windows-sys/windows-targets version changes. Either explain in the PR description why the bump is required for the Android back-navigation change (for example, a `handleBackNavigation` API that exists only in 0.53.4), or split the bump into its own PR. Do not change unrelated lockfile entries.

findings.title: No tests for the new API or Android back-press behaviour
findings.body:
Nothing in this PR tests `onBackButtonPress` or the Kotlin back-press dispatch. The TS wrapper has no unit test, and the Kotlin `AppPlugin` has no instrumentation test for the listener versus fallback branches. These are the branches most likely to break, and the Rust `setup` compile error above would have been caught by an Android build in CI.

::diff{file="packages/api/src/app.ts" lines="267-277"}
findings.fixPrompt: Add tests for the new back-button feature. In `packages/api`, add a unit test that `onBackButtonPress` calls `addPluginListener` with plugin 'app' and event 'back-button' (mock `invoke`). In the Android module, add a unit test covering `AppPlugin`'s `handleOnBackPressed` with and without a registered `back-button` listener, asserting the trigger, goBack, and default-activity paths. Follow the existing test layout in the repo.

findings.title: Removed imports in Plugin.kt and path/android.rs are unused
findings.body: The PR drops `android.os.Bundle` and `org.json.JSONException` from `Plugin.kt`, and `std::ffi::OsStr` from `path/android.rs`. I confirmed that none of these names is referenced in those files, so the import cleanup is correct and does not break the build.

findings.title: hasListener helper and TS payload type are clean additions
findings.body: `hasListener` in `Plugin.kt` is a small, well-placed helper that reuses the existing `listeners` map and mirrors the null-safe style of `trigger`. The TS side exports a named `OnBackButtonPressPayload` type and reuses `addPluginListener<T>`, which keeps the typed payload consistent with the Kotlin `canGoBack` field.
